definitions.explanation: A moderate, balanced stance that avoids extremes. Used in politics to describe centrist positions, and in Buddhism to refer to the Middle Way — the path between indulgence and asceticism.

examples.japanese: {中道|ちゅうどう}の{立場|たちば}を{取|と}る。
その{政党|せいとう}は{中道|ちゅうどう}{路線|ろせん}を{掲|かか}げている。
examples.english: That political party advocates a centrist line.

examples.japanese: {左右|さゆう}の{極端|きょくたん}な{意見|いけん}を{避|さ}け、{中道|ちゅうどう}を{歩|あゆ}むことが{大切|たいせつ}だと{考|かんが}えている。
examples.english: I believe it is important to avoid extreme opinions on either side and walk the middle path.

notes:
Compound noun: {中|ちゅう} (middle) + {道|どう} (way, path). Used in both political and Buddhist contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中道|ちゅうどう}{路線|ろせん} (centrist line/policy)
- {中道|ちゅうどう}{政党|せいとう} (centrist party)
- {中道|ちゅうどう}{右派|うは}/{左派|さは} (center-right/center-left)
- {中道|ちゅうどう}を{歩|あゆ}む (to walk the middle path)

CULTURE:
In Buddhism, {中道|ちゅうどう} refers to the Middle Way taught by the Buddha — avoiding both extreme self-indulgence and extreme asceticism.
